newsitem.title: USA: Doe Run postpones $175 mln junk deal-sources.
newsitem.headline: Doe Run postpones $175 mln junk deal-sources.

text.p: Doe Run Co has postponed a planned $175 million junk bond offering in the U.S. as the company weighs its options on whether to purchase a metallurgic complex in Peru, according to market sources.
Peru's state miner Centromin said Friday it had given purchase rights of the La Oroya metallurgic complex to Doe Run following a decision by Mexico's Penoles to withraw its offer.
Calls to Renco Group, the parent company of Doe Run, were not immediately returned.
Doe Run, the largest integrated lead producer in the U.S. was runner-up to Penoles in an April 18 auction for rights to La Oroya.
"The company is now considering whether to do the acquisition and investigating why Penoles pulled out," said a source close to the situation.
The source added, "(Doe Run) might issue bonds to finance the acqusition if they go ahead with it. Either way, they are only postponing the deal temporarily."
Doe Run had planned to sell $175 million in seven-year senior notes in a 144a private placement via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette. DLJ officials did not immediately return calls.
